landmarks.info: About 350 m tall and shaped like a lotus bud. Opened in 2019.
Seafront promenade laid out in 1859 under Governor Sir Henry Ward.
Home of Parliament until 1982, now the Presidential Secretariat. Exterior only.
Founded in 1864, one of the oldest hotels in Asia.
Twin 39-storey towers in Fort, completed in 1997.
Clock tower from 1857 that also worked as a lighthouse until 1952.
Dutch-era hospital building, thought to be among the oldest in Fort. Now shops and restaurants.
Colombo's main railway station, opened in 1917.
The red-and-white mosque on Second Cross Street, Pettah, completed in 1909.
Buddhist temple by Beira Lake, founded in the late 1800s.
Meditation hall on Beira Lake, designed by Geoffrey Bawa.
Two residential towers, one leaning against the other.
Pettah's clock tower at the top of Main Street.
White domed home of the Colombo Municipal Council, opened in 1928.
Colombo's largest park, formerly Victoria Park.
Sri Lanka's largest museum, founded in 1877.
Built for the ceremonial opening of Parliament after independence in 1948, modelled on a Kandyan royal audience hall.
Restored colonial buildings, once a lunatic asylum and auditors' offices, now shops and cafes.
Dutch Reformed church completed in 1757, one of the oldest Protestant churches in the country.
Catholic shrine visited by people of every faith. Rebuilt after the 2019 Easter Sunday attack.
The largest church in Sri Lanka, in Kotahena, completed in 1906.
Hindu temple in Kotahena built in granite in the early 1900s.
Hindu temple on Galle Road, Bambalapitiya, starting point of the Vel festival procession.
Mosque and shrine opposite Town Hall, more than a century old.
Stupa raised on arches above the road near the port, built in 1956.
A Dutch-era belfry in Pettah that marked the old gate to the fort.
A 17th-century Dutch townhouse on Prince Street, Pettah.
Market stalls on walkways over Beira Lake beside the bus stand.
Hotel, homes and shops on the lakefront in Slave Island, opened in 2024.
New land reclaimed from the sea west of Fort and Galle Face.
International cricket ground in Maligawatte, seating about 35,000.
Athletics stadium near the Kelani river, built for the 1991 South Asian Games.
Former horse racing track from the 1890s, now a rugby ground and shopping arcade.
Performing arts theatre shaped like a lotus pond, opened in 2011.
Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall, opened in 1973.
The oldest university in Sri Lanka, in Cinnamon Gardens.
One of the first shopping malls in Colombo, in Kollupitiya.
Shopping mall on Galle Road, Bambalapitiya, opened in the 1980s.
Road bridges over the Kelani river at the north edge of the city.
Lake at the heart of the city, dating back to the Portuguese period.
